thread:
wanda: heads-up — ran into a reproducible dup-write on emulator API 34 using kotlin SDK + retrofit/okhttp. Sending a streaming POST (non-repeatable RequestBody) and hitting 401 triggers a retry that ends up sending the same payload twice.
lee: yikes. streaming body as in chunked upload that can't be replayed?
wanda: yes. our uploader reads from an InputStream and writes directly to sink. if auth refresh occurs mid-upload, okhttp retries or replays and server sees duplicate records. seen on Pixel 8 emulator.
max: do you have a minimal snippet of the RequestBody?
wanda: trimmed:```kotlin
class StreamBody(val src: InputStream): RequestBody() {
  override fun contentType() = "application/octet-stream".toMediaType()
  override fun writeTo(sink: BufferedSink) { src.source().use { it.readAll(sink) } }
}
```
lee: classic non-repeatable body issue. Also check how Authenticator performs refresh — if it blocks on the same OkHttpClient dispatcher, you can starve threads and cause weird retries.
wanda: our Authenticator does a blocking retrofit call (runBlocking -> suspend refresh). suspect that's part of it. logs show socket reset -> auth refresh -> second POST with same body bytes.
max: two straightforward fixes: 1) make bodies repeatable (buffer to temp file / ByteArray) so retries are safe, or 2) disable retryOnConnectionFailure for the uploader client and handle retries at a higher layer. also: use a dedicated OkHttpClient for auth refresh so you don't block the main dispatcher's threads.
lee: example disable:```kotlin
val client = OkHttpClient.Builder().retryOnConnectionFailure(false).build()
```
max: and dedicated auth client:```kotlin
val authClient = OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .dispatcher(Dispatcher().apply { maxRequests = 1 })
  .build()
val authRetrofit = Retrofit.Builder().client(authClient)...build()
```
wanda: tried both locally — buffering to file works but increases latency and disk IO; disabling retries stopped duplicates in the quick repro; dedicated auth client removed the dispatcher starvation case.
lee: also recommend idempotency-key header server-side for uploads that mutate state, so duplicates are safe. add that to devex docs.
wanda: opened a tiny repro in the kotlin-sdk-repros repo and added an emulator test that toggles retryOnConnectionFailure and simulates mid-upload 401: https://github.com/redwood-inference/kotlin-sdk-repros/pull/101
ci-bot: CI run 1789 for branch streaming-dup-fix started: https://ci.redwood.dev/build/1789 :eyes:
max: docs action: add a short "Non-repeatable RequestBody -> duplicate side-effects" note in devex onboarding with recommended patterns (buffer, disable retry, dedicated auth client, idempotency). I'll draft the PR and link the repro.
wanda: thanks — saved someone from a bad dataloss weekend. :relieved:
